questions.q: Do all liquids conduct electricity? Explain the chemical effects of electric current.

answer.text: Not all liquids conduct electricity. Solutions of acids, bases and salts, such as salt water and lemon juice, conduct well because they contain charged particles called ions. Distilled water, sugar solution and oil are poor conductors. A simple tester with an LED can show whether a liquid conducts.

When an electric current passes through a conducting liquid, it can cause chemical changes, known as the chemical effect of current. These effects include the formation of gas bubbles at the electrodes, the deposition of a metal on an electrode, and changes in the colour of the solution.

answer: This chemical effect is the basis of electrolysis and of electroplating.

questions.q: What is electroplating, and what are its uses?
answer: Electroplating is the process of depositing a layer of one metal over another metal using the chemical effect of electric current.

answer.text: The object to be plated is made the cathode, the plating metal forms the anode, and the solution contains a salt of the plating metal. When current flows, the metal is deposited evenly over the object.

Chromium is plated on taps and car parts to make them shiny and rust-resistant. Silver and gold are plated on cheaper metals for jewellery and decoration. Tin is plated on iron cans, as tin is non-toxic, to store food safely, and zinc is coated on iron in galvanisation to prevent rusting.

answer: Electroplating thus improves appearance, prevents corrosion and saves costly metals.
